(hp : AllocPre s space base size align) (freeAuth : Option Nat) :
    Aligned (s.alloc space base size align freeAuth) := by
  obtain ⟨-, h0, h2, hm, -⟩ := hp
  intro i a ha
  simp only [State.alloc] at ha
  split at ha
  · cases ha
    exact ⟨h0, h2, hm⟩
  · exact h i a ha

section StepTheorems

variable {Ty : Type}

/-- An `ok` raw write preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §20.2 ¶2). -/
theorem WriteStep_admissible {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (h : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s'))
    (hs : Admissible s) : Admissible s' := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 h
  exact ⟨write_wf hs.wf ac w, liveDisjoint_write hs.disjoint ac w, aligned_write hs.aligned ac w⟩

/-- An `ok` raw deallocation preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §20.2 ¶2). -/
theorem DeallocStep_admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State}
    (h : DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s')) (hs : Admissible s) : Admissible s' := by
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 h
  exact ⟨dealloc_wf hs.wf id, liveDisjoint_dealloc hs.disjoint id,
    aligned_dealloc hs.aligned id⟩

/-- An `ok` raw creation preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §9 ¶11, §20.2 ¶2). -/
theorem AllocStep_admissible {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat}
    {s s' : State} (h : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok s'))
    (hs : Admissible s) : Admissible s' := by
  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := AllocStep_ok_iff.1 h
  exact ⟨alloc_wf hs.wf space base size align freeAuth, liveDisjoint_alloc hs.disjoint hp freeAuth,
    aligned_alloc hs.aligned hp freeAuth⟩

/-- Every `ok` step preserves admissibility (§9 ¶8, §20.2 ¶2). -/
theorem Step.admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') (hs : Admissible s) :
    Admissible s' := by
  cases h with
  | read _ => exact hs
  | write h => exact WriteStep_admissible h hs
  | dealloc h => exact DeallocStep_admissible h hs
  | alloc h => exact AllocStep_admissible h hs

/-- Every state of an execution from an admissible initial state is admissible
(§9 ¶8, §9 ¶9). -/
theorem Exec.admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s₀ s : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s₀ s) (h₀ : Admissible s₀) :
    Admissible s := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact h₀
  | cons hs _ ih => exact ih (hs.admissible h₀)

/-- Every state reachable from an admissible initial state is admissible (§9 ¶9). -/
theorem Reachable.admissible {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {s₀ s : State} (h : Reachable C ObR ObW s₀ s)
    (h₀ : Admissible s₀) : Admissible s :=
  let ⟨_, he⟩ := h
  he.admissible h₀

/-- Frame of an `ok` raw write (§16 ¶3, §13 ¶3): other allocations unchanged; in the target
only bytes change, and only inside the written range; the counter is unchanged. -/
theorem WriteStep_frame {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (h : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s')) :
    (∀ i, i ≠ ac.prov → s'.allocs i = s.allocs i) ∧
    (∃ a a', s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ s'.allocs ac.prov = some a' ∧
      { a' with bytes := a.bytes } = a ∧
      ∀ j, ¬ (ac.addr - a.base ≤ j ∧ j < ac.addr - a.base + ac.len) → a'.bytes j = a.bytes j) ∧
    s'.next = s.next := by
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, -⟩, -⟩, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 h
  refine ⟨fun i hi => by simp only [State.write]; exact ite_eq_right hi,
    ⟨a, a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, ha, ?_, rfl,
      fun j hj => Alloc.write_bytes_out a w hj⟩, rfl⟩
  rw [State.write_allocs_self, ha]
  rfl

/-- Frame of an `ok` raw deallocation (§17 ¶3, §13): other allocations unchanged; the target
only becomes dead and stays registered; the counter is unchanged. -/
theorem DeallocStep_frame {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s s' : State}
    (h : DeallocStep C id auth s (.ok s')) :
    (∀ i, i ≠ id → s'.allocs i = s.allocs i) ∧
    (∃ a, s.allocs id = some a ∧ s'.allocs id = some { a with live := false }) ∧
    s'.next = s.next := by
  obtain ⟨⟨a, ha, -⟩, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 h
  refine ⟨fun i hi => by simp only [State.dealloc]; exact ite_eq_right hi, ⟨a, ha, ?_⟩, rfl⟩
  rw [State.dealloc_allocs_self, ha]
  rfl

/-- Frame of an `ok` raw creation (§13 ¶3, §9 ¶11, §10 ¶5): the identity `s.next` was
unregistered, every other entry is unchanged, the new allocation is live and wholly
uninitialized, and the counter advances. -/
theorem AllocStep_frame {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s s' : State}
    (h : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s (.ok s')) :
    s.allocs s.next = none ∧ (∀ i, i ≠ s.next → s'.allocs i = s.allocs i) ∧
    s'.allocs s.next =
      some { space, base, size, align, live := true, bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth } ∧
    s'.next = s.next + 1 := by
  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := AllocStep_ok_iff.1 h
  exact ⟨hp.1, fun i hi => by simp only [State.alloc]; exact ite_eq_right hi,
    State.alloc_allocs_self s space base size align freeAuth, rfl⟩

/-! ## Liveness, invalidation, identities across executions (§13, §15.1, §16.1, §17) -/

/-- An `ok` raw read resolves to a live allocation (§15.1). -/
theorem read_requires_live {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
    {v : List AByte} (h : ReadStep ObR ac t s (.ok v)) :
    ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true :=
  let ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, hl, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩ := ReadStep_ok_iff.1 h
  ⟨a, ha, hl⟩

/-- An `ok` raw write resolves to a live allocation (§16.1). -/
theorem write_requires_live {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (h : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s')) :
    ∃ a, s.allocs ac.prov = some a ∧ a.live = true :=
  let ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, hl, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 h
  ⟨a, ha, hl⟩

/-- A raw read through the provenance of a dead allocation is `ub` (§15.1, §17 ¶3). -/
theorem ReadStep_dead {R : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State} {a : Alloc}
    {o : ReadOutcome} (ha : s.allocs ac.prov = some a) (hd : a.live = false)
    (h : ReadStep R ac t s o) : o = .ub := by
  cases h with
  | ok _ hc =>
    obtain ⟨b, hb, hl, _⟩ := hc.1
    rw [ha] at hb
    cases hb
    rw [hd] at hl
    exact nomatch hl
  | ub => rfl

/-- A raw write through the provenance of a dead allocation is `ub` (§16.1, §17 ¶3). -/
theorem WriteStep_dead {W : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s : State} {a : Alloc} {o : Outcome}
    (ha : s.allocs ac.prov = some a) (hd : a.live = false) (h : WriteStep W ac t w s o) :
    o = .ub := by
  cases h with
  | ok hc =>
    obtain ⟨b, hb, hl, _⟩ := hc.1
    rw [ha] at hb
    cases hb
    rw [hd] at hl
    exact nomatch hl
  | ub => rfl

/-- A raw deallocation of a dead allocation is `ub` (§17.1, §17 ¶3). -/
theorem DeallocStep_dead {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {id auth : Nat} {s : State} {a : Alloc}
    {o : Outcome} (ha : s.allocs id = some a) (hd : a.live = false)
    (h : DeallocStep C id auth s o) : o = .ub := by
  cases h with
  | ok hc =>
    obtain ⟨b, hb, hl, _⟩ := hc
    rw [ha] at hb
    cases hb
    rw [hd] at hl
    exact nomatch hl
  | ub => rfl

/-- An `ok` step that neither writes through `i` nor deallocates `i` leaves the registered
entry `i` unchanged (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3). -/
theorem Step.keeps {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
    (hk : op.KeepsAlloc i) (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : s'.allocs i = some a := by
  cases h with
  | read _ => exact ha
  | @write ac _ w _ _ hw =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 hw
    have hk : ac.prov ≠ i := hk
    simp only [State.write]
    rw [ite_eq_right (Ne.symm hk)]
    exact ha
  | @dealloc id _ _ _ hd =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 hd
    have hk : id ≠ i := hk
    simp only [State.dealloc]
    rw [ite_eq_right (Ne.symm hk)]
    exact ha
  | alloc hal =>
    obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := AllocStep_ok_iff.1 hal
    have hne : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hp.1] at ha; cases ha
    simp only [State.alloc]
    rw [ite_eq_right hne]
    exact ha

/-- No `ok` step writes through or deallocates a dead allocation (§16.1, §17.1). -/
theorem Step.keepsAlloc_of_dead {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') {i : Nat}
    {a : Alloc} (ha : s.allocs i = some a) (hd : a.live = false) : op.KeepsAlloc i := by
  cases h with
  | read _ => trivial
  | @write ac _ _ _ _ hw =>
    show ac.prov ≠ i
    intro e
    rw [← e] at ha
    exact nomatch WriteStep_dead ha hd hw
  | @dealloc id _ _ _ hdl =>
    show id ≠ i
    intro e
    rw [← e] at ha
    exact nomatch DeallocStep_dead ha hd hdl
  | alloc _ => trivial

/-- An `ok` step keeps every registered identity registered (§13 ¶1). -/
theorem Step.registered {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {op : Op Ty} {s s' : State} (h : Step C ObR ObW op s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
    (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : ∃ a', s'.allocs i = some a' := by
  cases h with
  | read _ => exact ⟨a, ha⟩
  | @write ac _ w _ _ hw =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 hw
    simp only [State.write]
    split
    · exact ⟨_, by rw [ha]; rfl⟩
    · exact ⟨a, ha⟩
  | @dealloc id _ _ _ hd =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := DeallocStep_ok_iff.1 hd
    simp only [State.dealloc]
    split
    · exact ⟨_, by rw [ha]; rfl⟩
    · exact ⟨a, ha⟩
  | alloc hal => exact ⟨a, (Step.alloc (C := C) (ObR := ObR) (ObW := ObW) hal).keeps trivial ha⟩

/-- Along an execution whose operations neither write through `i` nor deallocate `i`, the
registered entry `i` is unchanged (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §16 ¶5). -/
theorem Exec.keeps {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
    (hk : ∀ op ∈ ops, op.KeepsAlloc i) (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : s'.allocs i = some a := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact ha
  | cons hs _ ih =>
    exact ih (fun op hop => hk op (List.Mem.tail _ hop)) (hs.keeps (hk _ (List.Mem.head _)) ha)

/-- A dead allocation stays registered and dead, unchanged, in every later state of an
execution (§13 ¶1). -/
theorem dead_persists {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
    (ha : s.allocs i = some a) (hd : a.live = false) : s'.allocs i = some a := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact ha
  | cons hs _ ih => exact ih (hs.keeps (hs.keepsAlloc_of_dead ha hd) ha)

/-- A registered identity stays registered in every later state of an execution
(§13 ¶1). -/
theorem Exec.registered {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' : State} (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc}
    (ha : s.allocs i = some a) : ∃ a', s'.allocs i = some a' := by
  induction h generalizing a with
  | nil => exact ⟨a, ha⟩
  | cons hs _ ih =>
    obtain ⟨a', ha'⟩ := hs.registered ha
    exact ih ha'

/-- An identity registered at some point of an execution is never assigned again by a later
creation (§13 ¶1). -/
theorem alloc_identity_never_reused {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ops : List (Op Ty)} {s s' s'' : State}
    (h : Exec C ObR ObW ops s s') {i : Nat} {a : Alloc} (ha : s.allocs i = some a)
    {space base size align : Nat} {freeAuth : Option Nat}
    (hal : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s' (.ok s'')) : i ≠ s'.next := by
  intro e
  obtain ⟨a', ha'⟩ := h.registered ha
  rw [e, (AllocStep_frame hal).1] at ha'
  cases ha'

/-- After an `ok` raw deallocation of `i`, in every later state of an execution, every
raw read and every raw write through provenance `i` is `ub` (§17 ¶3, §13 ¶2). -/
theorem dealloc_invalidates {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {i auth : Nat} {s s₁ s₂ : State} {ops : List (Op Ty)}
    (hd : DeallocStep C i auth s (.ok s₁)) (he : Exec C ObR ObW ops s₁ s₂) {ac : Access}
    (hp : ac.prov = i) :
    (∀ (R : ReadOblSpec Ty) (t : Ty) (o : ReadOutcome), ReadStep R ac t s₂ o → o = .ub) ∧
    (∀ (W : WriteOblSpec Ty) (t : Ty) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (o : Outcome),
      WriteStep W ac t w s₂ o → o = .ub) := by
  obtain ⟨-, ⟨a, -, ha⟩, -⟩ := DeallocStep_frame hd
  have h₂ : s₂.allocs ac.prov = some { a with live := false } := hp ▸ dead_persists he ha rfl
  exact ⟨fun _ _ _ hr => ReadStep_dead h₂ rfl hr, fun _ _ _ _ hw => WriteStep_dead h₂ rfl hw⟩

/-- No double free: after an `ok` raw deallocation of `i`, every raw deallocation of `i`
in a later state of an execution is `ub`, whatever the authority and compatibility relation
(§17 ¶3). -/
theorem no_double_free {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {i auth : Nat} {s s₁ s₂ : State} {ops : List (Op Ty)}
    (hd : DeallocStep C i auth s (.ok s₁)) (he : Exec C ObR ObW ops s₁ s₂) :
    ∀ (C' : Nat → Nat → Prop) (auth' : Nat) (o : Outcome), DeallocStep C' i auth' s₂ o → o = .ub := by
  obtain ⟨-, ⟨a, -, ha⟩, -⟩ := DeallocStep_frame hd
  exact fun _ _ _ h => DeallocStep_dead (dead_persists he ha rfl) rfl h

/-- Reuse does not restore: after an `ok` raw deallocation of `i` and an `ok` raw
creation, possibly at the same base, raw reads and writes through provenance `i` stay `ub`
in every later state (§13 ¶2, §12 ¶3). -/
theorem reuse_does_not_restore {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {i auth : Nat} {space base size align : Nat}
    {freeAuth : Option Nat} {s s₁ s₂ s₃ : State} {ops : List (Op Ty)}
    (hd : DeallocStep C i auth s (.ok s₁))
    (hal : AllocStep space base size align freeAuth s₁ (.ok s₂))
    (he : Exec C ObR ObW ops s₂ s₃) {ac : Access} (hp : ac.prov = i) :
    (∀ (R : ReadOblSpec Ty) (t : Ty) (o : ReadOutcome), ReadStep R ac t s₃ o → o = .ub) ∧
    (∀ (W : WriteOblSpec Ty) (t : Ty) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (o : Outcome),
      WriteStep W ac t w s₃ o → o = .ub) :=
  dealloc_invalidates hd (.cons (.alloc hal) he) hp

/-! ## Writes: initialization, read-after-write, non-interference (§16) -/

/-- After an `ok` raw write, the bytes of the written range are initialized with the
written values and provenance (§16 ¶2). -/
theorem write_initializes {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (h : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s')) :
    ∃ a', s'.allocs ac.prov = some a' ∧
      ∀ i, i < ac.len → a'.bytes (ac.addr - a'.base + i) = .init (w i).1 (w i).2 := by
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, -⟩, -⟩, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 h
  refine ⟨a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, ?_, fun i hi => Alloc.write_bytes_in a w hi⟩
  rw [State.write_allocs_self, ha]
  rfl

/-- When the kernel conditions of a read hold, its outcome depends only on the parametric
obligations, and an `ok` outcome carries the bytes of the accessed range (§15, §20.2 ¶1). -/
theorem ReadStep_iff_of_canRead {R : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ac : Access} {t : Ty} {s : State}
    {a : Alloc} (ha : s.allocs ac.prov = some a) (hc : CanRead s ac) (o : ReadOutcome) :
    ReadStep R ac t s o ↔
      (R.dec s ac t ∧ R.stat s ac t) ∧ o = .ok (a.bytesAt (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len) ∨
      ¬ (R.dec s ac t ∧ R.stat s ac t) ∧ o = .ub := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases h with
    | ok hb hcd =>
      rw [ha] at hb
      cases hb
      exact Or.inl ⟨⟨hcd.2.1, hcd.2.2⟩, rfl⟩
    | ub hn => exact Or.inr ⟨fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => hn ⟨hc, h1, h2⟩, rfl⟩
  · rintro (⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, rfl⟩ | ⟨hn, rfl⟩)
    · exact .ok ha ⟨hc, h1, h2⟩
    · exact .ub fun ⟨_, h1, h2⟩ => hn ⟨h1, h2⟩

/-- Read-after-write (§16 ¶5): after an `ok` raw write through `ac`, followed by an execution
with no write through the same provenance and no deallocation of the allocation, an access
`ac'` of the same provenance on any subrange of the written range satisfies the kernel read
conditions, and every raw read through it, at any type and under any obligations, is `ok`
with exactly the corresponding written bytes, provenance included, when the obligations hold,
and `ub` otherwise. -/
theorem write_read_sub {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : ReadOblSpec Ty} {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty}
    {ac ac' : Access} {t : Ty} {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s₁ s₂ : State}
    {ops : List (Op Ty)} (hw : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s₁)) (he : Exec C ObR ObW ops s₁ s₂)
    (hk : ∀ op ∈ ops, op.KeepsAlloc ac.prov)
    (hp : ac'.prov = ac.prov) (h1 : ac.addr ≤ ac'.addr)
    (h2 : ac'.addr + ac'.len ≤ ac.addr + ac.len) :
    CanRead s₂ ac' ∧ ∀ (R : ReadOblSpec Ty) (t' : Ty) (o : ReadOutcome),
      ReadStep R ac' t' s₂ o ↔
        (R.dec s₂ ac' t' ∧ R.stat s₂ ac' t') ∧
          o = .ok (writtenBytes w (ac'.addr - ac.addr) ac'.len) ∨
        ¬ (R.dec s₂ ac' t' ∧ R.stat s₂ ac' t') ∧ o = .ub := by
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, hl, hsp, -⟩, -⟩, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 hw
  have h₁ : (s.write ac w).allocs ac.prov = some (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) := by
    rw [State.write_allocs_self, ha]
    rfl
  have h₂ : s₂.allocs ac'.prov = some (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) :=
    hp ▸ he.keeps hk h₁
  have key : ∀ i, i < ac'.len → (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w).bytes
      (ac'.addr - a.base + i) = .init (w (ac'.addr - ac.addr + i)).1
        (w (ac'.addr - ac.addr + i)).2 := by
    intro i hi
    have hb := hsp.1
    have e : ac'.addr - a.base + i = (ac.addr - a.base) + (ac'.addr - ac.addr + i) := by omega
    rw [e, Alloc.write_bytes_in a w (by omega)]
  have hR : CanRead s₂ ac' :=
    ⟨_, h₂, hl, ⟨Nat.le_trans hsp.1 h1, Nat.le_trans h2 hsp.2⟩, fun i hi => by
      show (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w).bytes (ac'.addr - a.base + i) ≠ .uninit
      rw [key i hi]
      nofun, Or.inl rfl⟩
  refine ⟨hR, fun R t' o => ?_⟩
  have hv : (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w).bytesAt
      (ac'.addr - (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w).base) ac'.len =
      writtenBytes w (ac'.addr - ac.addr) ac'.len :=
    List.map_congr_left fun i hi => key i (List.mem_range.1 hi)
  rw [← hv]
  exact ReadStep_iff_of_canRead h₂ hR o

/-- Non-interference (§16 ¶5): an `ok` raw write through `ac` changes neither the kernel read
conditions nor the result of a valid read through `ac'` when `ac'` has another provenance or
a range disjoint from the written range. -/
theorem write_noninterference {ObW : WriteOblSpec Ty} {ac ac' : Access} {t : Ty}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} {s s' : State} (hw : WriteStep ObW ac t w s (.ok s'))
    (hd : ac'.prov ≠ ac.prov ∨ RangeDisjoint ac.addr ac.len ac'.addr ac'.len) :
    (CanRead s' ac' ↔ CanRead s ac') ∧
      ∀ (R : ReadOblSpec Ty) (t' : Ty) (v v' : List AByte),
        ReadStep R ac' t' s (.ok v) → ReadStep R ac' t' s' (.ok v') → v = v' := by
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨a, ha, -, hsp, -⟩, -⟩, rfl⟩ := WriteStep_ok_iff.1 hw
  by_cases hp : ac'.prov = ac.prov
  · have hr : RangeDisjoint ac.addr ac.len ac'.addr ac'.len := hd.resolve_left (· hp)
    have ha' : s.allocs ac'.prov = some a := hp ▸ ha
    have hwa : (s.write ac w).allocs ac'.prov = some (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) := by
      rw [hp, State.write_allocs_self, ha]
      rfl
    have key : Spatial a ac' → ∀ i, i < ac'.len →
        (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w).bytes (ac'.addr - a.base + i) =
          a.bytes (ac'.addr - a.base + i) := by
      intro hs' i hi
      apply Alloc.write_bytes_out
      intro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      obtain ⟨hb, -⟩ := hsp
      obtain ⟨hb', -⟩ := hs'
      exact hr (ac'.addr + i) (by omega) (by omega) (by omega) (by omega)
    refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, fun R t' v v' h h' => ?_⟩
    · rintro ⟨b, hb, hl', hs', hi', hau⟩
      rw [hwa] at hb
      cases hb
      exact ⟨a, ha', hl', hs', fun i hi => by rw [← key hs' i hi]; exact hi' i hi, hau⟩
    · rintro ⟨b, hb, hl', hs', hi', hau⟩
      rw [ha'] at hb
      cases hb
      exact ⟨_, hwa, hl', hs', fun i hi => by
        show (a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w).bytes (ac'.addr - a.base + i) ≠ .uninit
        rw [key hs' i hi]
        exact hi' i hi, hau⟩
    · obtain ⟨⟨⟨b, hb, -, hs', -⟩, -⟩, b₁, hb₁, rfl⟩ := ReadStep_ok_iff.1 h
      obtain ⟨-, b₂, hb₂, rfl⟩ := ReadStep_ok_iff.1 h'
      rw [ha'] at hb hb₁
      cases hb
      cases hb₁
      rw [hwa] at hb₂
      cases hb₂
      exact (List.map_congr_left fun i hi => key hs' i (List.mem_range.1 hi)).symm
  · have he : (s.write ac w).allocs ac'.prov = s.allocs ac'.prov := by
      simp only [State.write]
      exact ite_eq_right hp
    refine ⟨by unfold CanRead; rw [he], fun R t' v v' h h' => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨-, b₁, hb₁, rfl⟩ := ReadStep_ok_iff.1 h
    obtain ⟨-, b₂, hb₂, rfl⟩ := ReadStep_ok_iff.1 h'
    rw [he, hb₁] at hb₂
    cases hb₂
    rfl

end StepTheorems

/-! ## Non-vacuity witnesses -/

namespace Witness

/-- Explicit test instance of the read obligations, both parts `True` (§20.3 ¶1: explicit
predicates, chosen here, not tacitly replaced). -/
def obR : ReadObl Unit :=
  { dec := fun _ _ _ => True, stat := fun _ _ _ => True, decInst := fun _ _ _ => instDecidableTrue }

/-- Explicit test instance of the write obligations, both parts `True` (§20.3 ¶1). -/
def obW : WriteObl Unit :=
  { dec := fun _ _ _ _ => True, stat := fun _ _ _ _ => True,
    decInst := fun _ _ _ _ => instDecidableTrue }

/-- A state with one live allocation, identity `0`, base `96`, size `8`, alignment `8`,
deallocation token `7` (§9 ¶1). -/
def s₁ : State := State.empty.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7)

/-- Write access to the first 4 bytes of allocation `0` (§12 ¶1). -/
def acW : Access := ⟨96, 0, 4, .write⟩

/-- Read access to the first 4 bytes of allocation `0` (§12 ¶1). -/
def acR : Access := ⟨96, 0, 4, .read⟩

/-- Written representation: value `i + 1`, no provenance, at position `i` (§10 ¶2). -/
def w₀ : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat := fun i => (i.toUInt8 + 1, none)

/-- `s₁` after the write of `w₀` through `acW` (§16 ¶2). -/
def s₂ : State := s₁.write acW w₀

/-- Non-vacuity (§9 ¶9, §16, §15, §20.2 ¶1): `s₁` is reached from the empty state, is
admissible and has a live allocation; a raw write through `acW` is `ok` and leads to `s₂`; a
raw read through `acR` in `s₂` is `ok` with the written bytes, by the relation and by the
interpreter. -/
theorem nonvacuous :
    Exec (· = ·) obR.toSpec obW.toSpec [.alloc 0 96 8 8 (some 7), .write acW () w₀]
      State.empty s₂ ∧
    Admissible s₁ ∧ (∃ a, s₁.allocs 0 = some a ∧ a.live = true) ∧
    WriteStep obW.toSpec acW () w₀ s₁ (.ok s₂) ∧
    ReadStep obR.toSpec acR () s₂ (.ok [.init 1 none, .init 2 none, .init 3 none, .init 4 none]) ∧
    read obR acR () s₂ trivial = .ok [.init 1 none, .init 2 none, .init 3 none, .init 4 none] := by
  have hal : AllocStep 0 96 8 8 (some 7) State.empty (.ok s₁) :=
    .ok ((allocPreDec_iff admissible_empty.wf).1 (by decide))
  have hw : WriteStep obW.toSpec acW () w₀ s₁ (.ok s₂) := .ok ⟨by decide, trivial, trivial⟩
  have hr : read obR acR () s₂ trivial =
      .ok [.init 1 none, .init 2 none, .init 3 none, .init 4 none] := by decide
  exact ⟨.cons (.alloc hal) (.cons (.write hw) (.nil _)), AllocStep_admissible hal admissible_empty,
    ⟨_, rfl, rfl⟩, hw, read_sound hr, hr⟩

/-- Non-vacuity of `reuse_does_not_restore` (§13 ¶2): from `s₂`, allocation `0` is
deallocated with a compatible token, then a new allocation is created at the same base `96`;
both steps are `ok`, the new allocation is live at base `96`, and the old read access is
`ub`. -/
theorem reuse_nonvacuous :
    ∃ s₃ s₄, DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 s₂ (.ok s₃) ∧ AllocStep 0 96 8 8 none s₃ (.ok s₄) ∧
      (∃ b, s₄.allocs 1 = some b ∧ b.live = true ∧ b.base = 96) ∧
      ReadStep obR.toSpec acR () s₄ .ub := by
  have hd : DeallocStep (· = ·) 0 7 s₂ (.ok (s₂.dealloc 0)) := .ok (by decide)
  have hwf : WF (s₂.dealloc 0) :=
    (DeallocStep_admissible hd (WriteStep_admissible nonvacuous.2.2.2.1 nonvacuous.2.1)).wf
  have hal : AllocStep 0 96 8 8 none (s₂.dealloc 0)
      (.ok ((s₂.dealloc 0).alloc 0 96 8 8 none)) :=
    .ok ((allocPreDec_iff hwf).1 (by decide))
  obtain ⟨o, ho⟩ := ReadStep_total_on obR acR () ((s₂.dealloc 0).alloc 0 96 8 8 none) trivial
  have hub := (reuse_does_not_restore (ObR := obR.toSpec) (ObW := obW.toSpec) hd hal (.nil _)
    (ac := acR) rfl).1 _ _ _ ho
  subst hub
  exact ⟨_, _, hd, hal, ⟨_, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, ho⟩

-- The read interpreter also runs in compiled code on the witness (§20.3 ¶3).
#guard read obR acR () s₂ trivial = .ok [.init 1 none, .init 2 none, .init 3 none, .init 4 none]

end Witness

end Ern.MemoryModel.Machine

7	Source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`, §82 (items 1–8) with §10, §16, §17, §23.
8	
9	* A layout of places in allocations and its interface `LayoutWF` (§82.1, §23).
10	* The representation relation `Repr` between a kernel state (`Access.S3`) and an admissible state
11	  of the memory machine (`Machine.State`, §9) (§82.1, §82.3, §82.4, §82.5).
12	* For every kernel operation O1–O16, the sequence of raw operations that realizes its `ok` step,
13	  proven to be a sequence of `ok` raw steps that keeps `Repr` (§82 preamble, §82.2, §82.4, §82.5).
14	* Safe reads and writes (§82.2), lifetimes (§82.5), deallocation contracts (§82.4), pinned
15	  addresses under pinning obligations (§82.6, §74, §75), exclusivity of bytes (§82.8), pointers
16	  written by `store` (§82.2, §82.3), every region included.
17	* A simulation of runs from the initial state with parameters fixed once per run, and concrete
18	  runs checked by evaluation. On reachable states (§57, `Access.reachable_kinv`) the per-step
19	  results hold without invariant hypotheses (`*_reachable`).
20	
21	The sequential fragment only (§18, §29): no theorem here says anything about concurrency.
22	-/

28	/-! ## Allocations of the memory machine (§9) -/
29	
30	/-- The allocation `i` of `s2` is registered and satisfies `p` (§9, §11 ¶2). -/
31	def AllocP (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) (p : Machine.Alloc → Prop) : Prop :=
32	  ∃ a, s2.allocs i = some a ∧ p a
33	
34	/-- The allocation `i` of `s2` is registered and live (§9 ¶1, §17 ¶3). -/
35	abbrev LiveAlloc (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) : Prop := AllocP s2 i (·.live = true)
36	
37	/-- Weakening of the property of a registered allocation (§9). -/
38	theorem AllocP.mono {s : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p q : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
39	    (h : AllocP s i p) (hpq : ∀ a, p a → q a) : AllocP s i q :=
40	  let ⟨a, ha, hp⟩ := h; ⟨a, ha, hpq a hp⟩
41	
42	/-- Two properties of one registered allocation (§9). -/
43	theorem AllocP.and {s : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p q : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
44	    (hp : AllocP s i p) (hq : AllocP s i q) : AllocP s i fun a => p a ∧ q a := by
45	  obtain ⟨a, ha, h1⟩ := hp
46	  obtain ⟨b, hb, h2⟩ := hq
47	  rw [ha] at hb; cases hb
48	  exact ⟨a, ha, h1, h2⟩
49	
50	/-- A registered allocation is below the counter of a state with fresh identities (§9 ¶7). -/
51	theorem AllocP.lt {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) {i : Nat} {p : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
52	    (h : AllocP s i p) : i < s.next :=
53	  Nat.lt_of_not_le fun hle => by obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h; rw [hwf i hle] at ha; cases ha
54	
55	/-- Base address of the allocation `i` of `s2`, `0` if unregistered (§9 ¶1, §12 ¶1). -/
56	def baseOf (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((s2.allocs i).map (·.base)).getD 0
57	
58	/-- The base of a registered allocation (§9 ¶1). -/
59	theorem baseOf_of {s2 : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {a : Machine.Alloc} (h : s2.allocs i = some a) :
60	    baseOf s2 i = a.base := by
61	  simp [baseOf, h]

63	/-! ## Layout of places (§82.1, §23) -/
64	
65	/-- Layout of places (§82.1): place `q` occupies the range `L q` of the elementary memory machine:
66	an allocation identity, an offset and a length (§11 ¶1). A parameter fixed for a run, defined on
67	every index, present or future. Only the allocation of a non-leaf place is read. -/
68	abbrev Layout := Nat → Machine.Place
69	
70	/-- Layout interface in the states `s3`, `s2` (§82.1; §23 "a memory layout satisfying
71	`LayoutWF`"). The spec names `LayoutWF` without stating its clauses; the clauses below are the
72	guarantees §82.1 and §23 ask the layout to provide. No lower bound on lengths: a leaf may have
73	size zero (§71.1). -/
74	structure LayoutWF (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) : Prop where
75	  /-- §82.1 (parts): a structural part lies in the allocation of its parent. -/
76	  parts : ∀ q r, parentOf s3.P q = some r → (L q).alloc = (L r).alloc
77	  /-- §23, §82.1 (disjointness): two distinct leaves in one allocation have disjoint ranges. -/
78	  disjoint : ∀ l l', l < s3.P.length → l' < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → isLeaf s3.P l' →
79	    l ≠ l' → (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc →
80	    Machine.RangeDisjoint (L l).off (L l).len (L l').off (L l').len
81	  /-- §82.1, §15 ¶1: the range of a leaf lies within its allocation, which is registered. -/
82	  within : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l →
83	    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size
84	
85	/-- Elements of a parent chain lie in the allocation of its start (§82.1 parts, §40). -/
86	theorem alloc_chainF {L : Layout} {P : List Place}
87	    (hp : ∀ q r, parentOf P q = some r → (L q).alloc = (L r).alloc) :
88	    ∀ k i r, r ∈ chainF (parentOf P) k i → (L i).alloc = (L r).alloc
89	  | 0, _, _, h => by simp [chainF] at h
90	  | k + 1, i, r, h => by
91	    simp only [chainF] at h
92	    split at h
93	    · rename_i o ho
94	      split at h
95	      · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
96	        · exact hp i _ ho
97	        · exact (hp i o ho).trans (alloc_chainF hp k o r h)
98	      · simp at h
99	    · simp at h
100	
101	/-- A part lies in the allocation of every place it belongs to (§82.1 parts, §40). -/
102	theorem LayoutWF.alloc_part {L : Layout} {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} (hl : LayoutWF L s3 s2)
103	    {l r : Nat} (h : partOf s3.P l r) : (L l).alloc = (L r).alloc := by
104	  rcases h.2 with rfl | h
105	  · rfl
106	  · exact alloc_chainF hl.parts l l r h
107	
108	/-! ## Representation relation (§82.1, §82.3, §82.4, §82.5, §9) -/
109	
110	/-- Representation relation between a kernel state `s3` and a state `s2` of the memory machine,
111	for the layout `L` and the deallocation tokens `rtok` recorded for the allocation of each root
112	place (`rtok r` for the root place `r`; §17 ¶4, §70.2):
113	- `adm`: `s2` is admissible (§9 ¶8: freshness, live disjointness, alignment);
114	- `layout`: the layout interface (§82.1, §23);
115	- `inj`: two distinct root places are in distinct allocations (§82.1: storage units and
116	  identities; §9 ¶5: subplaces are not new allocations, so parts share their root's);
117	- `tokens`: the allocation of a root place is registered and records the token `rtok r`
118	  (§82.4, §17 ¶4);
119	- `live`: the allocation of a usable root place is live (§82.5);
120	- `init`: the bytes of the range of an `Init` leaf are initialized (§82.3; `Uninit` and `Moved`
121	  impose nothing, §41).
122	It does not read the contract `K` (§48). -/
123	structure Repr (L : Layout) (rtok : Nat → Nat) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) : Prop where
124	  /-- §9 ¶8: admissibility of the memory state. -/
125	  adm : Machine.Admissible s2
126	  /-- §82.1, §23: layout interface. -/
127	  layout : LayoutWF L s3 s2
128	  /-- §82.1, §9 ¶5: distinct root places, distinct allocations. -/
129	  inj : ∀ r r', RootPlace s3.P r → RootPlace s3.P r' → r ≠ r' → (L r).alloc ≠ (L r').alloc
130	  /-- §82.4, §17 ¶4: the allocation of a root place is registered with the token `rtok r`. -/
131	  tokens : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → AllocP s2 (L r).alloc fun a => a.freeAuth = some (rtok r)
132	  /-- §82.5: the allocation of a usable root place is live. -/
133	  live : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → s3.Usable r → LiveAlloc s2 (L r).alloc
134	  /-- §82.3: the range of an `Init` leaf is initialized. -/
135	  init : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3.I l = .init →
136	    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len
137	
138	/-! ## Sequences of raw operations (§20.1, §20.3) -/
139	
140	section Seq
141	
142	variable {Ty : Type}
143	
144	/-- Effect of an `ok` raw operation (§20.2): a read leaves the state unchanged. -/
145	def opEff : Machine.Op Ty → Machine.State → Machine.State
146	  | .read _ _, s => s
147	  | .write ac _ w, s => s.write ac w
148	  | .dealloc id _, s => s.dealloc id
149	  | .alloc sp b sz al fa, s => s.alloc sp b sz al fa
150	
151	/-- State after a sequence of `ok` raw operations (§20.3 ¶3). -/
152	def run : Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Machine.State
153	  | s, [] => s
154	  | s, o :: os => run (opEff o s) os
155	
156	/-- `p s o` holds for each operation `o` of the sequence in the state where it runs (§20.3). -/
157	def Along (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) :
158	    Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Prop
159	  | _, [] => True
160	  | s, o :: os => p s o ∧ Along p (opEff o s) os
161	
162	/-- Decidability of `Along` for a decidable property (§20.3 ¶3). -/
163	instance decAlong (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) [h : ∀ s o, Decidable (p s o)] :
164	    (s : Machine.State) → (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) → Decidable (Along p s os)
165	  | _, [] => isTrue trivial
166	  | s, o :: os => @instDecidableAnd _ _ (h s o) (decAlong p (opEff o s) os)
167	
168	/-- The parametric obligations of a raw read or write hold, both parts (§15 ¶5, §16 ¶4,
169	§20.3 ¶1): explicit predicates of the execution context, never replaced by `True`. -/
170	def Obl (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (s : Machine.State) :
171	    Machine.Op Ty → Prop
172	  | .read ac t => ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t
173	  | .write ac t w => ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w
174	  | _ => True
175	
176	/-- The parametric obligations hold for every read and write of a sequence, in the state where it
177	runs (§20.3). -/
178	abbrev OblAlong (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) :
179	    Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Prop :=
180	  Along (Obl ObR ObW)
181	
182	/-- The operation is an `ok` raw step from `s` to its effect (§20.1 ¶2). -/
183	def OkAt (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty)
184	    (s : Machine.State) (o : Machine.Op Ty) : Prop :=
185	  Machine.Step C ObR ObW o s (opEff o s)
186	
187	/-- A sequence of operations each `ok` where it runs is an execution (§20.3 ¶3). -/
188	theorem exec_of_along {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
189	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} :
190	    ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s os →
191	      Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os s (run s os)
192	  | [], s, _ => .nil s
193	  | _ :: os, _, ⟨h, hs⟩ => .cons h (exec_of_along os _ hs)
194	
195	/-- Composition of sequences (§20.3 ¶3). -/
196	theorem run_append (s : Machine.State) (os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)) :
197	    run s (os ++ os') = run (run s os) os' := by
198	  induction os generalizing s with
199	  | nil => rfl
200	  | cons o os ih => exact ih _
201	
202	/-- `Along` over a composed sequence (§20.3 ¶3). -/
203	theorem along_append {p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop} {s : Machine.State}
204	    {os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)} :
205	    Along p s (os ++ os') ↔ Along p s os ∧ Along p (run s os) os' := by
206	  induction os generalizing s with
207	  | nil => simp [Along, run]
208	  | cons o os ih => simp only [List.cons_append, Along, run, ih, and_assoc]
209	
210	/-- Executions compose (§20.3 ¶3). -/
211	theorem exec_append {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
212	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)} {s s' s'' : Machine.State}
213	    (h : Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os s s') (h' : Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os' s' s'') :
214	    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (os ++ os') s s'' := by
215	  induction h with
216	  | nil => exact h'
217	  | cons hs _ ih => exact .cons hs (ih h')
218	
219	end Seq

221	/-! ## Allocations kept by raw operations (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3) -/
222	
223	/-- `s'` keeps every allocation of `s` registered, with its base, size and deallocation token, and
224	every initialized byte initialized; liveness is not constrained (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶2, §16 ¶3,
225	§17 ¶3). -/
226	def Dom (s s' : Machine.State) : Prop :=
227	  ∀ i a, s.allocs i = some a → ∃ a', s'.allocs i = some a' ∧ a'.base = a.base ∧
228	    a'.size = a.size ∧ a'.freeAuth = a.freeAuth ∧ ∀ j, a.bytes j ≠ .uninit → a'.bytes j ≠ .uninit
229	
230	/-- `Dom` is reflexive (§13). -/
231	theorem Dom.refl (s : Machine.State) : Dom s s :=
232	  fun _ a h => ⟨a, h, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
233	
234	/-- `Dom` is transitive (§13). -/
235	theorem Dom.trans {s s' s'' : Machine.State} (h : Dom s s') (h' : Dom s' s'') : Dom s s'' := by
236	  intro i a ha
237	  obtain ⟨a', ha', e1, e2, e3, hb⟩ := h i a ha
238	  obtain ⟨a'', ha'', f1, f2, f3, hb'⟩ := h' i a' ha'
239	  exact ⟨a'', ha'', f1.trans e1, f2.trans e2, f3.trans e3, fun j hj => hb' j (hb j hj)⟩
240	
241	/-- Transport of a property of a registered allocation along `Dom` (§13 ¶3). -/
242	theorem AllocP.dom {s s' : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
243	    (h : AllocP s i p) (hd : Dom s s')
244	    (hp : ∀ a a' : Machine.Alloc, a'.base = a.base → a'.size = a.size →
245	      a'.freeAuth = a.freeAuth → (∀ j, a.bytes j ≠ .uninit → a'.bytes j ≠ .uninit) →
246	      p a → p a') :
247	    AllocP s' i p := by
248	  obtain ⟨a, ha, hpa⟩ := h
249	  obtain ⟨a', ha', e1, e2, e3, hb⟩ := hd i a ha
250	  exact ⟨a', ha', hp a a' e1 e2 e3 hb hpa⟩
251	
252	/-- Initialized ranges stay initialized along `Dom` (§16 ¶2). -/
253	theorem AllocP.dom_init {s s' : Machine.State} {i off len : Nat}
254	    (h : AllocP s i fun a => a.InitRange off len) (hd : Dom s s') :
255	    AllocP s' i fun a => a.InitRange off len :=
256	  h.dom hd fun _ _ _ _ _ hb h j hj => hb _ (h j hj)
257	
258	/-- Allocation entries after a write (§16 ¶2, ¶3). -/
259	theorem write_allocs (s : Machine.State) (ac : Machine.Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
260	    (i : Nat) :
261	    (s.write ac w).allocs i = if i = ac.prov then
262	      (s.allocs i).map (fun a => a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) else s.allocs i := rfl
263	
264	/-- Allocation entries after a deallocation (§17 ¶3). -/
265	theorem dealloc_allocs (s : Machine.State) (id i : Nat) :
266	    (s.dealloc id).allocs i = if i = id then
267	      (s.allocs i).map (fun a => { a with live := false }) else s.allocs i := rfl
268	
269	/-- Allocation entries after a creation (§9 ¶11, §13 ¶3). -/
270	theorem alloc_allocs (s : Machine.State) (sp b sz al : Nat) (fa : Option Nat) (i : Nat) :
271	    (s.alloc sp b sz al fa).allocs i = if i = s.next then
272	      some { space := sp, base := b, size := sz, align := al, live := true,
273	             bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth := fa } else s.allocs i := rfl
274	
275	section Keep
276	
277	variable {Ty : Type}
278	
279	/-- Every `ok` effect keeps the allocations of a state with fresh identities (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3,
280	§17 ¶3). -/
281	theorem dom_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (o : Machine.Op Ty) :
282	    Dom s (opEff o s) := by
283	  intro i a ha
284	  cases o with
285	  | read => exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
286	  | write ac t w =>
287	    show ∃ a', (s.write ac w).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
288	    rw [write_allocs]
289	    split
290	    · refine ⟨a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, by rw [ha]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun j hj => ?_⟩
291	      simp only [Machine.Alloc.write]
292	      split
293	      · exact fun h => by cases h
294	      · exact hj
295	    · exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
296	  | dealloc id au =>
297	    show ∃ a', (s.dealloc id).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
298	    rw [dealloc_allocs]
299	    split
300	    · exact ⟨{ a with live := false }, by rw [ha]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
301	    · exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
302	  | alloc sp b sz al fa =>
303	    show ∃ a', (s.alloc sp b sz al fa).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
304	    have hi : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hwf s.next (Nat.le_refl _)] at ha; cases ha
305	    rw [alloc_allocs, ite_eq_right hi]
306	    exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
307	
308	/-- Every `ok` effect keeps freshness (§9 ¶7). -/
309	theorem wf_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (o : Machine.Op Ty) :
310	    Machine.WF (opEff o s) := by
311	  cases o with
312	  | read => exact hwf
313	  | write ac t w => exact Machine.write_wf hwf ac w
314	  | dealloc id au => exact Machine.dealloc_wf hwf id
315	  | alloc sp b sz al fa => exact Machine.alloc_wf hwf sp b sz al fa
316	
317	/-- Every sequence of `ok` effects keeps freshness (§9 ¶7). -/
318	theorem wf_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
319	    Machine.WF (run s os)
320	  | [], _, h => h
321	  | o :: os, _, h => wf_run os _ (wf_opEff h o)
322	
323	/-- Every sequence of `ok` effects keeps the allocations (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3). -/
324	theorem dom_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
325	    Dom s (run s os)
326	  | [], s, _ => Dom.refl s
327	  | o :: os, _, h => (dom_opEff h o).trans (dom_run os _ (wf_opEff h o))
328	
329	/-- An operation that deallocates no identity: a read, a write or a creation (§13 ¶3,
330	§16 ¶3). -/
331	def NoDealloc : Machine.Op Ty → Prop
332	  | .dealloc .. => False
333	  | _ => True
334	
335	/-- An effect other than a deallocation keeps every live allocation live (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3). -/
336	theorem live_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) {o : Machine.Op Ty}
337	    (ho : NoDealloc o) {i : Nat} (h : LiveAlloc s i) : LiveAlloc (opEff o s) i := by
338	  obtain ⟨a, ha, hl⟩ := h
339	  cases o with
340	  | read => exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
341	  | write ac t w =>
342	    show AllocP (s.write ac w) i _
343	    rw [AllocP, write_allocs]
344	    split
345	    · exact ⟨a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, by rw [ha]; simp, hl⟩
346	    · exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
347	  | dealloc => exact ho.elim
348	  | alloc sp b sz al fa =>
349	    have hi : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hwf s.next (Nat.le_refl _)] at ha; cases ha
350	    show AllocP (s.alloc sp b sz al fa) i _
351	    rw [AllocP, alloc_allocs, ite_eq_right hi]
352	    exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
353	
354	/-- A sequence without deallocation keeps every live allocation live (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3). -/
355	theorem live_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
356	    (∀ o ∈ os, NoDealloc o) → ∀ {i : Nat}, LiveAlloc s i → LiveAlloc (run s os) i
357	  | [], _, _, _, _, h => h
358	  | o :: os, _, hwf, hn, _, h =>
359	    live_run os _ (wf_opEff hwf o) (fun o' ho' => hn o' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ho'))
360	      (live_opEff hwf (hn o (List.mem_cons_self ..)) h)
361	
362	/-- The base of a registered allocation is kept by every sequence of `ok` effects (§13 ¶3: no
363	allocation moves). -/
364	theorem baseOf_run {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) {i : Nat}
365	    (h : AllocP s i fun _ => True) : baseOf (run s os) i = baseOf s i := by
366	  obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h
367	  obtain ⟨a', ha', e, -⟩ := dom_run os s hwf i a ha
368	  rw [baseOf_of ha, baseOf_of ha', e]
369	
370	end Keep
371	
372	/-! ## Transport of `Repr` -/
373	
374	/-- `Repr` carries over to a kernel state with the same tree of places (same number of places
375	and same parents) and a memory state that keeps the allocations (`Dom`) and is admissible, when
376	every usable root place of the new state has a live allocation and every leaf that becomes `Init`
377	has its range initialized (§82.1, §82.3, §82.5). -/
378	theorem Repr.transport {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 s2' : Machine.State}
379	    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hadm : Machine.Admissible s2') (hd : Dom s2 s2')
380	    (hlen : s3'.P.length = s3.P.length) (hpar : parentOf s3'.P = parentOf s3.P)
381	    (hlive : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → s3'.Usable r → LiveAlloc s2' (L r).alloc)
382	    (hI : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3'.I l = .init →
383	      s3.I l = .init ∨ AllocP s2' (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len) :
384	    Repr L rtok s3' s2' := by
385	  have hleaf : ∀ l, isLeaf s3'.P l ↔ isLeaf s3.P l := fun l => by simp only [isLeaf, hlen, hpar]
386	  have hroot : ∀ r, RootPlace s3'.P r ↔ RootPlace s3.P r := fun r => by
387	    simp only [RootPlace, hlen, hpar]
388	  refine ⟨hadm, ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
389	  · intro q r h; rw [hpar] at h; exact hR.layout.parts q r h
390	  · intro l l' hl hl' hf hf' hne he
391	    rw [hlen] at hl hl'; rw [hleaf] at hf hf'
392	    exact hR.layout.disjoint l l' hl hl' hf hf' hne he
393	  · intro l hl hf

395	    exact (hR.layout.within l hl hf).dom hd fun _ _ _ e _ _ h => e ▸ h
396	  · intro r r' hr hr' hne

398	  · intro r hr

402	  · intro l hl hf hi

506	      Machine.ReadStep ObR (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l) s2
507	        (.ok (al.bytesAt (L l).off (L l).len)) := by
508	  obtain ⟨hlP, hlf, hu⟩ := leaf_of_leafOfUsable hw (hpre.usable l hl)

520	    ∀ ls t, run t (readOps s2 L ty ls) = t
521	  | [], _ => rfl
522	  | _ :: ls, t => run_readOps s2 L ty ls t

527	theorem r6_read {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
528	    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat}

531	    (hob : OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) :
532	    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (readOps s2 L ty ls) s2 (run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) ∧
533	      run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls) = s2 ∧ Repr L rtok s3' (run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) := by
534	  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h

538	      Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls') := by
539	    intro ls'
540	    induction ls' with
541	    | nil => intro _ _; trivial
542	    | cons l ls' ih =>
543	      intro hsub hob'
544	      obtain ⟨al, hal, -, -, hst⟩ := r1_read hR hw hpre (hsub l (List.mem_cons_self ..)) hob'.1
545	      exact ⟨.read hst, ih (fun l' hl' => hsub l' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hl')) hob'.2⟩

547	  rwa [run_readOps] at this

import Ern.MemoryModel.Machine
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main

/-!
# Refinement of the access kernel into the elementary memory machine (spec v0.1, Part XVII)

Source: `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`, §82 (items 1–8) with §10, §16, §17, §23.

* A layout of places in allocations and its interface `LayoutWF` (§82.1, §23).
* The representation relation `Repr` between a kernel state (`Access.S3`) and an admissible state
  of the memory machine (`Machine.State`, §9) (§82.1, §82.3, §82.4, §82.5).
* For every kernel operation O1–O16, the sequence of raw operations that realizes its `ok` step,
  proven to be a sequence of `ok` raw steps that keeps `Repr` (§82 preamble, §82.2, §82.4, §82.5).
* Safe reads and writes (§82.2), lifetimes (§82.5), deallocation contracts (§82.4), pinned
  addresses under pinning obligations (§82.6, §74, §75), exclusivity of bytes (§82.8), pointers
  written by `store` (§82.2, §82.3), every region included.
* A simulation of runs from the initial state with parameters fixed once per run, and concrete
  runs checked by evaluation. On reachable states (§57, `Access.reachable_kinv`) the per-step
  results hold without invariant hypotheses (`*_reachable`).

The sequential fragment only (§18, §29): no theorem here says anything about concurrency.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Refinement

open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Allocations of the memory machine (§9) -/

/-- The allocation `i` of `s2` is registered and satisfies `p` (§9, §11 ¶2). -/
def AllocP (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) (p : Machine.Alloc → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ a, s2.allocs i = some a ∧ p a

/-- The allocation `i` of `s2` is registered and live (§9 ¶1, §17 ¶3). -/
abbrev LiveAlloc (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) : Prop := AllocP s2 i (·.live = true)

/-- Weakening of the property of a registered allocation (§9). -/
theorem AllocP.mono {s : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p q : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
    (h : AllocP s i p) (hpq : ∀ a, p a → q a) : AllocP s i q :=
  let ⟨a, ha, hp⟩ := h; ⟨a, ha, hpq a hp⟩

/-- Two properties of one registered allocation (§9). -/
theorem AllocP.and {s : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p q : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
    (hp : AllocP s i p) (hq : AllocP s i q) : AllocP s i fun a => p a ∧ q a := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, h1⟩ := hp
  obtain ⟨b, hb, h2⟩ := hq
  rw [ha] at hb; cases hb
  exact ⟨a, ha, h1, h2⟩

/-- A registered allocation is below the counter of a state with fresh identities (§9 ¶7). -/
theorem AllocP.lt {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) {i : Nat} {p : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
    (h : AllocP s i p) : i < s.next :=
  Nat.lt_of_not_le fun hle => by obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h; rw [hwf i hle] at ha; cases ha

/-- Base address of the allocation `i` of `s2`, `0` if unregistered (§9 ¶1, §12 ¶1). -/
def baseOf (s2 : Machine.State) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((s2.allocs i).map (·.base)).getD 0

/-- The base of a registered allocation (§9 ¶1). -/
theorem baseOf_of {s2 : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {a : Machine.Alloc} (h : s2.allocs i = some a) :
    baseOf s2 i = a.base := by
  simp [baseOf, h]

/-! ## Layout of places (§82.1, §23) -/

/-- Layout of places (§82.1): place `q` occupies the range `L q` of the elementary memory machine:
an allocation identity, an offset and a length (§11 ¶1). A parameter fixed for a run, defined on
every index, present or future. Only the allocation of a non-leaf place is read. -/
abbrev Layout := Nat → Machine.Place

/-- Layout interface in the states `s3`, `s2` (§82.1; §23 "a memory layout satisfying
`LayoutWF`"). The spec names `LayoutWF` without stating its clauses; the clauses below are the
guarantees §82.1 and §23 ask the layout to provide. No lower bound on lengths: a leaf may have
size zero (§71.1). -/
structure LayoutWF (L : Layout) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) : Prop where
  /-- §82.1 (parts): a structural part lies in the allocation of its parent. -/
  parts : ∀ q r, parentOf s3.P q = some r → (L q).alloc = (L r).alloc
  /-- §23, §82.1 (disjointness): two distinct leaves in one allocation have disjoint ranges. -/
  disjoint : ∀ l l', l < s3.P.length → l' < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → isLeaf s3.P l' →
    l ≠ l' → (L l).alloc = (L l').alloc →
    Machine.RangeDisjoint (L l).off (L l).len (L l').off (L l').len
  /-- §82.1, §15 ¶1: the range of a leaf lies within its allocation, which is registered. -/
  within : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l →
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size

/-- Elements of a parent chain lie in the allocation of its start (§82.1 parts, §40). -/
theorem alloc_chainF {L : Layout} {P : List Place}
    (hp : ∀ q r, parentOf P q = some r → (L q).alloc = (L r).alloc) :
    ∀ k i r, r ∈ chainF (parentOf P) k i → (L i).alloc = (L r).alloc
  | 0, _, _, h => by simp [chainF] at h
  | k + 1, i, r, h => by
    simp only [chainF] at h
    split at h
    · rename_i o ho
      split at h
      · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
        · exact hp i _ ho
        · exact (hp i o ho).trans (alloc_chainF hp k o r h)
      · simp at h
    · simp at h

/-- A part lies in the allocation of every place it belongs to (§82.1 parts, §40). -/
theorem LayoutWF.alloc_part {L : Layout} {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} (hl : LayoutWF L s3 s2)
    {l r : Nat} (h : partOf s3.P l r) : (L l).alloc = (L r).alloc := by
  rcases h.2 with rfl | h
  · rfl
  · exact alloc_chainF hl.parts l l r h

/-! ## Representation relation (§82.1, §82.3, §82.4, §82.5, §9) -/

/-- Representation relation between a kernel state `s3` and a state `s2` of the memory machine,
for the layout `L` and the deallocation tokens `rtok` recorded for the allocation of each root
place (`rtok r` for the root place `r`; §17 ¶4, §70.2):
- `adm`: `s2` is admissible (§9 ¶8: freshness, live disjointness, alignment);
- `layout`: the layout interface (§82.1, §23);
- `inj`: two distinct root places are in distinct allocations (§82.1: storage units and
  identities; §9 ¶5: subplaces are not new allocations, so parts share their root's);
- `tokens`: the allocation of a root place is registered and records the token `rtok r`
  (§82.4, §17 ¶4);
- `live`: the allocation of a usable root place is live (§82.5);
- `init`: the bytes of the range of an `Init` leaf are initialized (§82.3; `Uninit` and `Moved`
  impose nothing, §41).
It does not read the contract `K` (§48). -/
structure Repr (L : Layout) (rtok : Nat → Nat) (s3 : S3) (s2 : Machine.State) : Prop where
  /-- §9 ¶8: admissibility of the memory state. -/
  adm : Machine.Admissible s2
  /-- §82.1, §23: layout interface. -/
  layout : LayoutWF L s3 s2
  /-- §82.1, §9 ¶5: distinct root places, distinct allocations. -/
  inj : ∀ r r', RootPlace s3.P r → RootPlace s3.P r' → r ≠ r' → (L r).alloc ≠ (L r').alloc
  /-- §82.4, §17 ¶4: the allocation of a root place is registered with the token `rtok r`. -/
  tokens : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → AllocP s2 (L r).alloc fun a => a.freeAuth = some (rtok r)
  /-- §82.5: the allocation of a usable root place is live. -/
  live : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → s3.Usable r → LiveAlloc s2 (L r).alloc
  /-- §82.3: the range of an `Init` leaf is initialized. -/
  init : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3.I l = .init →
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len

/-! ## Sequences of raw operations (§20.1, §20.3) -/

section Seq

variable {Ty : Type}

/-- Effect of an `ok` raw operation (§20.2): a read leaves the state unchanged. -/
def opEff : Machine.Op Ty → Machine.State → Machine.State
  | .read _ _, s => s
  | .write ac _ w, s => s.write ac w
  | .dealloc id _, s => s.dealloc id
  | .alloc sp b sz al fa, s => s.alloc sp b sz al fa

/-- State after a sequence of `ok` raw operations (§20.3 ¶3). -/
def run : Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Machine.State
  | s, [] => s
  | s, o :: os => run (opEff o s) os

/-- `p s o` holds for each operation `o` of the sequence in the state where it runs (§20.3). -/
def Along (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) :
    Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Prop
  | _, [] => True
  | s, o :: os => p s o ∧ Along p (opEff o s) os

/-- Decidability of `Along` for a decidable property (§20.3 ¶3). -/
instance decAlong (p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop) [h : ∀ s o, Decidable (p s o)] :
    (s : Machine.State) → (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) → Decidable (Along p s os)
  | _, [] => isTrue trivial
  | s, o :: os => @instDecidableAnd _ _ (h s o) (decAlong p (opEff o s) os)

/-- The parametric obligations of a raw read or write hold, both parts (§15 ¶5, §16 ¶4,
§20.3 ¶1): explicit predicates of the execution context, never replaced by `True`. -/
def Obl (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) (s : Machine.State) :
    Machine.Op Ty → Prop
  | .read ac t => ObR.dec s ac t ∧ ObR.stat s ac t
  | .write ac t w => ObW.dec s ac t w ∧ ObW.stat s ac t w
  | _ => True

/-- The parametric obligations hold for every read and write of a sequence, in the state where it
runs (§20.3). -/
abbrev OblAlong (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty) :
    Machine.State → List (Machine.Op Ty) → Prop :=
  Along (Obl ObR ObW)

/-- The operation is an `ok` raw step from `s` to its effect (§20.1 ¶2). -/
def OkAt (C : Nat → Nat → Prop) (ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty) (ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty)
    (s : Machine.State) (o : Machine.Op Ty) : Prop :=
  Machine.Step C ObR ObW o s (opEff o s)

/-- A sequence of operations each `ok` where it runs is an execution (§20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem exec_of_along {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} :
    ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Along (OkAt C ObR ObW) s os →
      Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os s (run s os)
  | [], s, _ => .nil s
  | _ :: os, _, ⟨h, hs⟩ => .cons h (exec_of_along os _ hs)

/-- Composition of sequences (§20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem run_append (s : Machine.State) (os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)) :
    run s (os ++ os') = run (run s os) os' := by
  induction os generalizing s with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons o os ih => exact ih _

/-- `Along` over a composed sequence (§20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem along_append {p : Machine.State → Machine.Op Ty → Prop} {s : Machine.State}
    {os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)} :
    Along p s (os ++ os') ↔ Along p s os ∧ Along p (run s os) os' := by
  induction os generalizing s with
  | nil => simp [Along, run]
  | cons o os ih => simp only [List.cons_append, Along, run, ih, and_assoc]

/-- Executions compose (§20.3 ¶3). -/
theorem exec_append {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {os os' : List (Machine.Op Ty)} {s s' s'' : Machine.State}
    (h : Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os s s') (h' : Machine.Exec C ObR ObW os' s' s'') :
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (os ++ os') s s'' := by
  induction h with
  | nil => exact h'
  | cons hs _ ih => exact .cons hs (ih h')

end Seq

/-! ## Allocations kept by raw operations (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3) -/

/-- `s'` keeps every allocation of `s` registered, with its base, size and deallocation token, and
every initialized byte initialized; liveness is not constrained (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶2, §16 ¶3,
§17 ¶3). -/
def Dom (s s' : Machine.State) : Prop :=
  ∀ i a, s.allocs i = some a → ∃ a', s'.allocs i = some a' ∧ a'.base = a.base ∧
    a'.size = a.size ∧ a'.freeAuth = a.freeAuth ∧ ∀ j, a.bytes j ≠ .uninit → a'.bytes j ≠ .uninit

/-- `Dom` is reflexive (§13). -/
theorem Dom.refl (s : Machine.State) : Dom s s :=
  fun _ a h => ⟨a, h, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩

/-- `Dom` is transitive (§13). -/
theorem Dom.trans {s s' s'' : Machine.State} (h : Dom s s') (h' : Dom s' s'') : Dom s s'' := by
  intro i a ha
  obtain ⟨a', ha', e1, e2, e3, hb⟩ := h i a ha
  obtain ⟨a'', ha'', f1, f2, f3, hb'⟩ := h' i a' ha'
  exact ⟨a'', ha'', f1.trans e1, f2.trans e2, f3.trans e3, fun j hj => hb' j (hb j hj)⟩

/-- Transport of a property of a registered allocation along `Dom` (§13 ¶3). -/
theorem AllocP.dom {s s' : Machine.State} {i : Nat} {p : Machine.Alloc → Prop}
    (h : AllocP s i p) (hd : Dom s s')
    (hp : ∀ a a' : Machine.Alloc, a'.base = a.base → a'.size = a.size →
      a'.freeAuth = a.freeAuth → (∀ j, a.bytes j ≠ .uninit → a'.bytes j ≠ .uninit) →
      p a → p a') :
    AllocP s' i p := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, hpa⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨a', ha', e1, e2, e3, hb⟩ := hd i a ha
  exact ⟨a', ha', hp a a' e1 e2 e3 hb hpa⟩

/-- Initialized ranges stay initialized along `Dom` (§16 ¶2). -/
theorem AllocP.dom_init {s s' : Machine.State} {i off len : Nat}
    (h : AllocP s i fun a => a.InitRange off len) (hd : Dom s s') :
    AllocP s' i fun a => a.InitRange off len :=
  h.dom hd fun _ _ _ _ _ hb h j hj => hb _ (h j hj)

/-- Allocation entries after a write (§16 ¶2, ¶3). -/
theorem write_allocs (s : Machine.State) (ac : Machine.Access) (w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat)
    (i : Nat) :
    (s.write ac w).allocs i = if i = ac.prov then
      (s.allocs i).map (fun a => a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w) else s.allocs i := rfl

/-- Allocation entries after a deallocation (§17 ¶3). -/
theorem dealloc_allocs (s : Machine.State) (id i : Nat) :
    (s.dealloc id).allocs i = if i = id then
      (s.allocs i).map (fun a => { a with live := false }) else s.allocs i := rfl

/-- Allocation entries after a creation (§9 ¶11, §13 ¶3). -/
theorem alloc_allocs (s : Machine.State) (sp b sz al : Nat) (fa : Option Nat) (i : Nat) :
    (s.alloc sp b sz al fa).allocs i = if i = s.next then
      some { space := sp, base := b, size := sz, align := al, live := true,
             bytes := fun _ => .uninit, freeAuth := fa } else s.allocs i := rfl

section Keep

variable {Ty : Type}

/-- Every `ok` effect keeps the allocations of a state with fresh identities (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3,
§17 ¶3). -/
theorem dom_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (o : Machine.Op Ty) :
    Dom s (opEff o s) := by
  intro i a ha
  cases o with
  | read => exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
  | write ac t w =>
    show ∃ a', (s.write ac w).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
    rw [write_allocs]
    split
    · refine ⟨a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, by rw [ha]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun j hj => ?_⟩
      simp only [Machine.Alloc.write]
      split
      · exact fun h => by cases h
      · exact hj
    · exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
  | dealloc id au =>
    show ∃ a', (s.dealloc id).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
    rw [dealloc_allocs]
    split
    · exact ⟨{ a with live := false }, by rw [ha]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
    · exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩
  | alloc sp b sz al fa =>
    show ∃ a', (s.alloc sp b sz al fa).allocs i = some a' ∧ _
    have hi : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hwf s.next (Nat.le_refl _)] at ha; cases ha
    rw [alloc_allocs, ite_eq_right hi]
    exact ⟨a, ha, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun _ h => h⟩

/-- Every `ok` effect keeps freshness (§9 ¶7). -/
theorem wf_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (o : Machine.Op Ty) :
    Machine.WF (opEff o s) := by
  cases o with
  | read => exact hwf
  | write ac t w => exact Machine.write_wf hwf ac w
  | dealloc id au => exact Machine.dealloc_wf hwf id
  | alloc sp b sz al fa => exact Machine.alloc_wf hwf sp b sz al fa

/-- Every sequence of `ok` effects keeps freshness (§9 ¶7). -/
theorem wf_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
    Machine.WF (run s os)
  | [], _, h => h
  | o :: os, _, h => wf_run os _ (wf_opEff h o)

/-- Every sequence of `ok` effects keeps the allocations (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3, §17 ¶3). -/
theorem dom_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
    Dom s (run s os)
  | [], s, _ => Dom.refl s
  | o :: os, _, h => (dom_opEff h o).trans (dom_run os _ (wf_opEff h o))

/-- An operation that deallocates no identity: a read, a write or a creation (§13 ¶3,
§16 ¶3). -/
def NoDealloc : Machine.Op Ty → Prop
  | .dealloc .. => False
  | _ => True

/-- An effect other than a deallocation keeps every live allocation live (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3). -/
theorem live_opEff {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) {o : Machine.Op Ty}
    (ho : NoDealloc o) {i : Nat} (h : LiveAlloc s i) : LiveAlloc (opEff o s) i := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, hl⟩ := h
  cases o with
  | read => exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
  | write ac t w =>
    show AllocP (s.write ac w) i _
    rw [AllocP, write_allocs]
    split
    · exact ⟨a.write (ac.addr - a.base) ac.len w, by rw [ha]; simp, hl⟩
    · exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩
  | dealloc => exact ho.elim
  | alloc sp b sz al fa =>
    have hi : i ≠ s.next := fun e => by rw [e, hwf s.next (Nat.le_refl _)] at ha; cases ha
    show AllocP (s.alloc sp b sz al fa) i _
    rw [AllocP, alloc_allocs, ite_eq_right hi]
    exact ⟨a, ha, hl⟩

/-- A sequence without deallocation keeps every live allocation live (§13 ¶3, §16 ¶3). -/
theorem live_run : ∀ (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) (s : Machine.State), Machine.WF s →
    (∀ o ∈ os, NoDealloc o) → ∀ {i : Nat}, LiveAlloc s i → LiveAlloc (run s os) i
  | [], _, _, _, _, h => h
  | o :: os, _, hwf, hn, _, h =>
    live_run os _ (wf_opEff hwf o) (fun o' ho' => hn o' (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ho'))
      (live_opEff hwf (hn o (List.mem_cons_self ..)) h)

/-- The base of a registered allocation is kept by every sequence of `ok` effects (§13 ¶3: no
allocation moves). -/
theorem baseOf_run {s : Machine.State} (hwf : Machine.WF s) (os : List (Machine.Op Ty)) {i : Nat}
    (h : AllocP s i fun _ => True) : baseOf (run s os) i = baseOf s i := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨a', ha', e, -⟩ := dom_run os s hwf i a ha
  rw [baseOf_of ha, baseOf_of ha', e]

end Keep

/-! ## Transport of `Repr` -/

/-- `Repr` carries over to a kernel state with the same tree of places (same number of places
and same parents) and a memory state that keeps the allocations (`Dom`) and is admissible, when
every usable root place of the new state has a live allocation and every leaf that becomes `Init`
has its range initialized (§82.1, §82.3, §82.5). -/
theorem Repr.transport {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 s2' : Machine.State}
    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hadm : Machine.Admissible s2') (hd : Dom s2 s2')
    (hlen : s3'.P.length = s3.P.length) (hpar : parentOf s3'.P = parentOf s3.P)
    (hlive : ∀ r, RootPlace s3.P r → s3'.Usable r → LiveAlloc s2' (L r).alloc)
    (hI : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3'.I l = .init →
      s3.I l = .init ∨ AllocP s2' (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len) :
    Repr L rtok s3' s2' := by
  have hleaf : ∀ l, isLeaf s3'.P l ↔ isLeaf s3.P l := fun l => by simp only [isLeaf, hlen, hpar]
  have hroot : ∀ r, RootPlace s3'.P r ↔ RootPlace s3.P r := fun r => by
    simp only [RootPlace, hlen, hpar]
  refine ⟨hadm, ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro q r h; rw [hpar] at h; exact hR.layout.parts q r h
  · intro l l' hl hl' hf hf' hne he
    rw [hlen] at hl hl'; rw [hleaf] at hf hf'
    exact hR.layout.disjoint l l' hl hl' hf hf' hne he
  · intro l hl hf
    rw [hlen] at hl; rw [hleaf] at hf
    exact (hR.layout.within l hl hf).dom hd fun _ _ _ e _ _ h => e ▸ h
  · intro r r' hr hr' hne
    exact hR.inj r r' ((hroot r).1 hr) ((hroot r').1 hr') hne
  · intro r hr
    exact (hR.tokens r ((hroot r).1 hr)).dom hd fun _ _ _ _ e _ h => e ▸ h
  · intro r hr hu
    exact hlive r ((hroot r).1 hr) hu
  · intro l hl hf hi
    rw [hlen] at hl; rw [hleaf] at hf
    rcases hI l hl hf hi with h | h
    · exact (hR.init l hl hf h).dom_init hd
    · exact h

/-! ## Accesses to leaves (§12, §15, §16) -/

/-- Address of the range of place `l` in `s2`: the base of its allocation plus its offset (§12 ¶1,
§82.1). -/
def leafAddr (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (l : Nat) : Nat := baseOf s2 (L l).alloc + (L l).off

/-- The means of access to the range of leaf `l` in `s2` (§12 ¶1, §82.2): address of the range,
provenance its allocation, length its size, elementary authority `au`. -/
def leafAcc (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (au : Machine.Auth) (l : Nat) : Machine.Access :=
  ⟨leafAddr s2 L l, (L l).alloc, (L l).len, au⟩

/-- The access to a leaf of a registered allocation (§12 ¶1). -/
theorem leafAcc_of {s2 : Machine.State} {L : Layout} {au : Machine.Auth} {l : Nat}
    {a : Machine.Alloc} (h : s2.allocs (L l).alloc = some a) :
    leafAcc s2 L au l = ⟨a.base + (L l).off, (L l).alloc, (L l).len, au⟩ := by
  simp [leafAcc, leafAddr, baseOf_of h]

/-- The access to a leaf is kept by `Dom` when its allocation is registered (§13 ¶3). -/
theorem leafAcc_dom {s2 s2' : Machine.State} (hd : Dom s2 s2') {L : Layout} {au : Machine.Auth}
    {l : Nat} (h : AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun _ => True) :
    leafAcc s2' L au l = leafAcc s2 L au l := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨a', ha', e, -⟩ := hd _ a ha
  rw [leafAcc_of ha, leafAcc_of ha', e]

/-- The kernel read conditions of the access to a leaf whose allocation is live, contains the
range and has it initialized (§15.1, §15.2, §15.3, §15.5). -/
theorem canRead_leaf {s2 : Machine.State} {L : Layout} {l : Nat} {a : Machine.Alloc}
    (ha : s2.allocs (L l).alloc = some a) (hl : a.live = true)
    (hs : (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size) (hi : a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len) :
    Machine.CanRead s2 (leafAcc s2 L .read l) := by
  rw [leafAcc_of ha]
  refine ⟨a, ha, hl, ⟨Nat.le_add_right _ _, by simp only; omega⟩, ?_, .inl rfl⟩
  simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]; exact hi

/-- The kernel write conditions of the access to a leaf whose allocation is live and contains the
range (§16.1, §16.2, §16.3). -/
theorem canWrite_leaf {s2 : Machine.State} {L : Layout} {l : Nat} {a : Machine.Alloc}
    (ha : s2.allocs (L l).alloc = some a) (hl : a.live = true)
    (hs : (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size) : Machine.CanWrite s2 (leafAcc s2 L .write l) := by
  rw [leafAcc_of ha]
  exact ⟨a, ha, hl, ⟨Nat.le_add_right _ _, by simp only; omega⟩, .inr rfl⟩

/-- After the write of the range of a leaf of a registered allocation, the range is initialized
(§16 ¶2). -/
theorem write_leaf_init {s2 : Machine.State} {L : Layout} {l : Nat}
    {w : Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat} (h : AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun _ => True) :
    AllocP (s2.write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) w) (L l).alloc
      fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len := by
  obtain ⟨a, ha, -⟩ := h
  refine ⟨a.write (L l).off (L l).len w, ?_, fun i hi => ?_⟩
  · rw [write_allocs, leafAcc_of ha]
    simp only [↓reduceIte, ha, Option.map_some, Nat.add_sub_cancel_left]
  · rw [Machine.Alloc.write_bytes_in a w hi]; exact fun h => by cases h

/-! ## Leaves of usable places -/

/-- A leaf of a usable place has a usable root place (§40, §49.2). -/
theorem root_of_leaf {s3 : S3} (hw : WF3 s3) {l : Nat} (hl : l < s3.P.length)
    (hu : s3.Usable l) : ∃ r, RootPlace s3.P r ∧ partOf s3.P l r ∧ s3.Usable r := by
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hlr⟩ := exists_rootPlace hw (l + 1) l (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hl
  exact ⟨r, hr, hlr, usable_of_part hw hlr hu⟩

/-- A leaf that belongs to a usable place is an existing usable leaf (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1,
§40). -/
theorem leaf_of_leafOfUsable {s3 : S3} (hw : WF3 s3) {l : Nat} (h : LeafOfUsable s3 l) :
    l < s3.P.length ∧ isLeaf s3.P l ∧ s3.Usable l := by
  obtain ⟨q, -, hq, hl⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨hlP, hlf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  exact ⟨hlP, hlf, usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hq⟩

/-- The allocation of a usable leaf is live and contains its range (§82.5, §82.1). -/
theorem Repr.leaf_live {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State}
    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) {l : Nat} (hl : l < s3.P.length)
    (hlf : isLeaf s3.P l) (hu : s3.Usable l) :
    AllocP s2 (L l).alloc fun a => a.live = true ∧ (L l).off + (L l).len ≤ a.size := by
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hlr, hur⟩ := root_of_leaf hw hl hu
  have hlive := hR.live r hr hur
  rw [← hR.layout.alloc_part hlr] at hlive
  exact hlive.and (hR.layout.within l hl hlf)

/-! ## R1: safe reads (§82.2, §66, §15) -/

/-- The reads realizing `read(access, ls)` (§82.2, §66): one raw read per leaf, of the range of
the leaf, at the type `ty l` of the leaf. -/
def readOps {Ty : Type} (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty) (ls : List Nat) :
    List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
  ls.map fun l => .read (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l)

/-- Safe read (§82.2, §66, §15): under `Repr`, `WF3` and the preconditions of `read` (§66), the
raw read of the range of each leaf read is `ok` when the parametric obligations of that read hold
(§15.4, §15.6, §15.7): its allocation is live, the range is initialized, and the read returns the
bytes of the range. -/
theorem r1_read {Ty : Type} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {L : Layout}
    {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat}
    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hw : WF3 s3) (hpre : Read3Pre s3 a ls) {l : Nat} (hl : l ∈ ls)
    (hob : ObR.dec s2 (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l) ∧ ObR.stat s2 (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l)) :
    ∃ al, s2.allocs (L l).alloc = some al ∧ al.live = true ∧ al.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len ∧
      Machine.ReadStep ObR (leafAcc s2 L .read l) (ty l) s2
        (.ok (al.bytesAt (L l).off (L l).len)) := by
  obtain ⟨hlP, hlf, hu⟩ := leaf_of_leafOfUsable hw (hpre.usable l hl)
  obtain ⟨al, hal, hlive, hsz⟩ := hR.leaf_live hw hlP hlf hu
  obtain ⟨al', hal', hi⟩ := hR.init l hlP hlf (hpre.init l hl)
  rw [hal] at hal'; cases hal'
  refine ⟨al, hal, hlive, hi, ?_⟩
  have hc := canRead_leaf hal hlive hsz hi
  have hst := Machine.ReadStep.ok (ObR := ObR) (t := ty l) hal ⟨hc, hob.1, hob.2⟩
  rw [leafAcc_of hal] at hst ⊢
  simpa only [Nat.add_sub_cancel_left] using hst

/-- The reads of a sequence of leaves leave the memory state unchanged (§20.2 ¶1). -/
theorem run_readOps {Ty : Type} (s2 : Machine.State) (L : Layout) (ty : Nat → Ty) :
    ∀ ls t, run t (readOps s2 L ty ls) = t
  | [], _ => rfl
  | _ :: ls, t => run_readOps s2 L ty ls t

/-- Realization of `read` (§82 preamble, §82.2, §66): under `Repr`, `WF3`, an `ok` step of `read`
and the parametric obligations along the reads, the reads form an execution of `ok` raw steps
that leaves the memory state unchanged, and `Repr` holds after the step. -/
theorem r6_read {Ty : Type} {C : Nat → Nat → Prop} {ObR : Machine.ReadOblSpec Ty}
    {ObW : Machine.WriteOblSpec Ty} {ty : Nat → Ty} {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat}
    {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2)
    (hw : WF3 s3) (h : Read3Step a ls s3 (.ok s3'))
    (hob : OblAlong ObR ObW s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) :
    Machine.Exec C ObR ObW (readOps s2 L ty ls) s2 (run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) ∧
      run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls) = s2 ∧ Repr L rtok s3' (run s2 (readOps s2 L ty ls)) := by
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  rw [run_readOps]
  refine ⟨?_, rfl, hR⟩

/-! ## Transport for steps that keep the places -/

/-- `Repr` carries over a step that keeps the places and makes no place usable, along raw steps
that keep the allocations and every live allocation live (§82.1, §82.3, §82.5). -/
theorem Repr.same_places {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 s2' : Machine.State}
    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hadm : Machine.Admissible s2') (hd : Dom s2 s2')
    (hl : ∀ i, LiveAlloc s2 i → LiveAlloc s2' i) (hP : s3'.P = s3.P)
    (hU : ∀ q, s3'.Usable q → s3.Usable q)
    (hI : ∀ l, l < s3.P.length → isLeaf s3.P l → s3'.I l = .init →
      s3.I l = .init ∨ AllocP s2' (L l).alloc fun a => a.InitRange (L l).off (L l).len) :
    Repr L rtok s3' s2' :=
  hR.transport hadm hd (by rw [hP]) (by rw [hP]) (fun r hr hu => hl _ (hR.live r hr (hU r hu))) hI

/-- `Repr` carries over a step that changes none of the places, the stack, the death markers and
the initialization states, with no raw operation (§82; §60–§62, §64, §74, §75: no storage
effect). -/
theorem Repr.of_eqs {L : Layout} {rtok : Nat → Nat} {s3 s3' : S3} {s2 : Machine.State}
    (hR : Repr L rtok s3 s2) (hP : s3'.P = s3.P) (hF : s3'.F = s3.F) (hd : s3'.dead = s3.dead)
    (hI : s3'.I = s3.I) : Repr L rtok s3' s2 :=
  hR.same_places hR.adm (Dom.refl _) (fun _ h => h) hP (fun _ h => h.of_eqs hP hF hd)
    fun _ _ _ h => .inl (hI ▸ h)

/-- The writes realizing `write(access, ls)` and `writeShared(access, ls)` (§82.2, §67, §68): one

    (w : Nat → Nat → UInt8 × Option Nat) (ls : List Nat) : List (Machine.Op Ty) :=
  ls.map fun l => .write (leafAcc s2 L .write l) (ty l) (w l)
